\documentclass[9pt]{extarticle}
\usepackage[margin=0.3in, landscape, top=0.2in, bottom=0.2in, left=0.2in, right=0.2in]{geometry}
\usepackage{amsmath, amssymb, enumitem, setspace}
\usepackage{mathrsfs}
\usepackage{mathtools}
\usepackage{parskip=0pt}

\begin{document}
\fontsize{7.5pt}{8.5pt}\selectfont

\textbf{MATH3033 Cheatsheet} \hfill \textit{Key Theorems, Definitions \& Formulas}

\hrule height 0.5pt

\section*{1. Infinite Series of Real Numbers}
\textbf{Defs:} $s_n=\sum_{k=1}^n a_k$. $\sum a_k$ converges to $s$: $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists N:n\ge N\implies|s_n-s|<\varepsilon$. Diverges: $\{s_n\}$ has no limit. Abs conv: $\sum|a_k|<\infty$. Conditional: conv but not abs.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Divergence Test (6.5):} $a_k\not\to0\implies\sum a_k$ diverges.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Geometric (6.7):} $\sum_{k=0}^\infty x^k=\frac1{1-x}$ for $|x|<1$, diverges for $|x|\ge1$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Cauchy Criterion (6.8):} $\sum a_k$ conv $\iff\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists N:m\ge n\ge N\implies\sum_{k=n}^m a_k<\varepsilon$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Comparison (6.14):} $0\le a_k\le b_k$ for large $k$: $\sum b_k<\infty\implies\sum a_k<\infty$; $\sum a_k=\infty\implies\sum b_k=\infty$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{LCT (6.16):} $L=\lim a_k/b_k$, $b_k>0$. $0<L<\infty$: same conv. $L=0$+$\sum b_k<\infty\implies\sum a_k<\infty$. $L=\infty$+$\sum b_k=\infty\implies\sum a_k=\infty$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Integral Test (6.12):} $f\ge0$ decr on $[1,\infty)$. $\sum f(k)$ conv $\iff\int_1^\infty f<\infty$. Cor 6.13: $\sum1/k^p$ conv $\iff p>1$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Root Test (6.23):} $r=\limsup|a_k|^{1/k}$. $r<1\implies$abs conv; $r>1\implies$diverge.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Ratio Test (6.24):} $r=\lim|a_{k+1}/a_k|$. $r<1\implies$abs conv; $r>1\implies$diverge.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Abs Conv (6.20):} Abs conv $\implies$conv (converse false). $\sum(-1)^k/k$ cond converges.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Rearrangements (6.27):} If $\sum a_k$ abs conv, every rearrangement $\to$ same sum. Riemann (6.29): Cond conv $\implies$ can rearrange to any $x\in\mathbb R\cup\{\pm\infty\}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Abel's Formula (6.30):} $A_{n,m}=\sum_{k=m}^n a_k$. $\sum_{k=m}^n a_kb_k=A_{n,m}b_n-\sum_{k=m}^{n-1}A_{k,m}(b_{k+1}-b_k)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Dirichlet's Test (6.31):} $\sum a_k$ partial sums bounded + $b_k\downarrow0$ $\implies\sum a_kb_k$ converges.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Alt Series Test (6.32):} $a_k\downarrow0\implies\sum(-1)^ka_k$ converges.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Alt Series Error (6.38):} $a_k\downarrow0$, $s=\sum(-1)^ka_k$, $|s-s_n|\le a_{n+1}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Integral Test Error (6.35):} $0\le\sum_{k=1}^n f(k)-\int_1^n f\le f(1)$. If $\sum f(k)$ conv: $0\le s-s_n+\int_n^\infty f\le f(n)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Logarithmic Test (6.42):} $p=\lim\frac{\log(1/|a_k|)}{\log k}$. $p>1\implies$abs conv; $p<1\implies$diverge.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Raabe's Test (6.43):} $|a_{k+1}/a_k|\le1-p/k+O(1/k)$ with $p>1\implies\sum a_k$ abs conv.

\section*{2. Infinite Series of Functions}
\textbf{Defs:} $f_n\to f$ ptwise: $\forall x\in E$, $\lim f_n(x)=f(x)$. Uniform: $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists N:n\ge N\implies|f_n(x)-f(x)|<\varepsilon\ \forall x\in E$ ($N$ depends only on $\varepsilon$, not $x$). Radius of conv $R$: series abs conv for $|x-x_0|<R$, diverges for $|x-x_0|>R$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Uniform $\Rightarrow$ Continuity (7.9):} $f_n\to f$ uniformly on $E$, each $f_n$ cont at $x_0\in E$ $\implies f$ cont at $x_0$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Uniform $\Rightarrow$ Integrability (7.10):} $f_n\to f$ uniformly on $[a,b]$, each integrable $\implies f$ integrable and $\int_a^b f_n\to\int_a^b f$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Uniform $\Rightarrow$ Differentiability (7.12):} $(a,b)$ bounded, $f_n$ diff on $(a,b)$, $f_n(x_0)$ converges for some $x_0$, $f_n'$ converges uniformly on $(a,b)\implies f_n\to f$ uniformly and $f'=\lim f_n'$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Uniform Cauchy Criterion (7.11):} $f_n$ conv uniformly on $E$ $\iff\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists N:n,m\ge N\implies|f_n(x)-f_m(x)|<\varepsilon\ \forall x\in E$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Weierstrass M-Test (7.15):} $|f_k(x)|\le M_k$ for $x\in E$, $\sum M_k<\infty\implies\sum f_k$ abs conv and uniformly on $E$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Term-by-Term Tests (7.14):} Uniform conv + each continuous $\implies\sum f_k$ continuous. On $[a,b]$, each integrable $\implies\int\sum f_k=\sum\int f_k$. Open interval, each diff, $\sum f_k$ conv at $x_0$, $\sum f_k'$ conv uniformly $\implies(\sum f_k)'=\sum f_k'$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Dirichlet's Test for Uniform Conv (7.16):} $|\sum_{k=1}^n f_k(x)|\le M$ for all $n,x\in E$ and $g_k\downarrow0$ uniformly $\implies\sum f_kg_k$ converges uniformly.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Power Series Radius (7.21):} $S(x)=\sum a_k(x-x_0)^k$, $R=1/\limsup|a_k|^{1/k}$. $S$ abs conv for $|x-x_0|<R$, uniformly on any $[a,b]\subset(x_0-R,x_0+R)$, diverges for $|x-x_0|>R$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{PS Diff \& Int (7.26,7.30,7.32):} On $(x_0-R,x_0+R)$, $S\in C^\infty$ and $S'(x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty k a_k(x-x_0)^{k-1}$, $\int S=\sum\frac{a_k}{k+1}(x-x_0)^{k+1}+C$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Abel's Theorem (7.27):} If $\sum a_k(x-x_0)^k$ converges on $[a,b]$, then it converges uniformly on $[a,b]$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Uniqueness (7.39):} If $f(x)=\sum a_k(x-x_0)^k$ on open interval $I$, then $a_k=f^{(k)}(x_0)/k!$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Binomial Series (7.52):} $|x|<1$, $(1+x)^\alpha=\sum_{k=0}^\infty\binom{\alpha}{k}x^k$, $\binom{\alpha}{k}=\frac{\alpha(\alpha-1)\cdots(\alpha-k+1)}{k!}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Key Series:} $e^x=\sum_{k=0}^\infty\frac{x^k}{k!}$, $\sin x=\sum_{k=0}^\infty\frac{(-1)^kx^{2k+1}}{(2k+1)!}$, $\cos x=\sum_{k=0}^\infty\frac{(-1)^kx^{2k}}{(2k)!}$, $\log(1+x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty\frac{(-1)^{k+1}x^k}{k}$, $|x|<1$.

\section*{3. Euclidean Spaces $\mathbb R^n$}

\textbf{Topological Definitions:}
\begin{itemize}[left=0pt, itemsep=0pt, topsep=0pt, parsep=0pt]
\item Open ball: $B_r(a)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x-a\|<r\}$. Closed ball: $\{\|x-a\|\le r\}$.
\item $V\subset\mathbb R^n$ is \textbf{open}: $\forall a\in V$, $\exists\varepsilon>0:B_\varepsilon(a)\subset V$.
\item $E$ is \textbf{closed}: $E^c$ is open.
\item \textbf{Relatively open in }$A$: $E\subset A$ is relatively open if $E=A\cap V$ for some open $V$.
\item \textbf{Relatively closed in }$A$: $E=A\cap F$ for some closed $F$.
\item \textbf{Compact}: every open cover has a finite subcover.
\item \textbf{Connected}: cannot be separated into two nonempty disjoint relatively-open sets.
\item \textbf{Interior} $E^\circ$: union of all open subsets of $E$ (largest open set $\subset E$).
\item \textbf{Closure} $\overline{E}$: intersection of all closed supersets of $E$ (smallest closed set $\supset E$).
\item \textbf{Boundary} $\partial E=\overline{E}\setminus E^\circ$.
\item \textbf{Limit point/accumulation point}: $x$ is limit point of $E$ if every $B_\varepsilon(x)$ contains $y\in E$ with $y\ne x$.
\item $E$ is \textbf{perfect}: $E$ is closed and every point of $E$ is a limit point of $E$.
\item \textbf{Dense}: $\overline{E}=\mathbb R^n$ (or $\overline{E}\cap U\neq\varnothing$ for every open $U$).
\item \textbf{Sequentially compact}: every sequence has a convergent subsequence.
\end{itemize}
\textbf{Cauchy-Schwarz (8.5):} $|x\cdot y|\le\|x\|\|y\|$, equality $\iff x,y$ parallel or one is zero.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Triangle Inequalities (8.6):} $\|x+y\|\le\|x\|+\|y\|$, $\|x-y\|\ge|\|x\|-\|y\||$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Norm Inequalities (8.7):} $\|x\|_\infty\le\|x\|\le\sqrt n\|x\|_\infty$, $\|x\|\le\|x\|_1\le\sqrt n\|x\|$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Heine-Borel (9.11):} $E\subset\mathbb R^n$ compact $\iff$ $E$ is closed and bounded.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Closed $\iff$ Sequential (9.8):} $E$ closed $\iff$ $x_k\in E$, $x_k\to x$ $\implies x\in E$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Limit Point Char:} $E$ closed $\iff$ $E$ contains all its limit points.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Open/Closed Properties (8.24):} Arbitrary unions of open are open; finite intersections of open are open. Arbitrary intersections of closed are closed; finite unions of closed are closed.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Connected $\iff$ Interval (8.30):} $E\subset\mathbb R$ connected $\iff$ $E$ is an interval. Rectangles in $\mathbb R^n$ are connected.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Linear Maps (8.15-8.18):} $T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ linear $\iff$ $T(x)=Bx$ for unique $m\times n$ matrix $B$. Operator norm: $\|T\|=\sup_{\|x\|=0}\frac{\|T(x)\|}{\|x\|}$, and $\|T(x)\|\le\|T\|\|x\|$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Cross Product (8.9):} $x,y\in\mathbb R^3$: $x\times y\perp x$ and $x\times y\perp y$. $\|x\times y\|=\|x\|\|y\|\sin\theta$. $x\times(y\times z)=(x\cdot z)y-(x\cdot y)z$.

\section*{4. Convergence in $\mathbb R^n$}
\textbf{Defs:} $x_k=(x_k^{(1)},\dots,x_k^{(n)})\to a=(a_1,\dots,a_n)\iff x_k^{(j)}\to a_j$ for each $j$. Bounded: $\exists M>0:\|x_k\|\le M\ \forall k$. Cauchy: $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists N:k,m\ge N\implies\|x_k-x_m\|<\varepsilon$.\\[-2pt]

$f(x)\to L$ as $x\to a$: $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists\delta>0:0<\|x-a\|<\delta\implies\|f(x)-L\|<\varepsilon$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Conv $\iff$ Componentwise (9.2):} $x_k^{(j)}\to a_j\ \forall j\iff x_k\to a$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Sequence Properties (9.4, 9.6):} Uniqueness. Subseq $\to$ same limit. Conv $\implies$ bounded. Conv $\iff$ Cauchy.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Bolzano-Weierstrass (9.5):} Every bounded sequence in $\mathbb R^n$ has a convergent subsequence.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Limit Laws (9.15):} $\lim(f+g)=L+M$, $\lim(\alpha f)=\alpha L$, $\lim(f\cdot g)=L\cdot M$. Squeeze: $g\le h\le f$, $\lim f=\lim g=L\implies\lim h=L$. Composition: $\lim_{x\to a}g(x)=L$, $\lim_{y\to L}h(y)=M\implies\lim_{x\to a}h(g(x))=M$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Limit $\iff$ Sequential (9.15ii):} $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=L\iff f(x_k)\to L$ for every $x_k\to a$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Continuous $\iff$ Preimage of Open (9.26):} $f:E\to\mathbb R^m$ continuous $\iff$ $f^{-1}(V)$ relatively open in $E$ for every open $V\subset\mathbb R^m$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Compact $\Rightarrow$ Continuity (9.29):} $K$ compact, $f:K\to\mathbb R^m$ continuous on $K$ $\implies f(K)$ compact. Hence $f$ bounded and attains max/min (Extreme Value Thm 9.32).\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Continuity $\Rightarrow$ Connectedness (9.30):} $E$ connected, $f:E\to\mathbb R^m$ continuous $\implies f(E)$ is connected.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Continuous Inverse (9.33):} $K$ compact, $f:K\to\mathbb R^m$ is 1-1 and continuous $\implies f^{-1}$ continuous on $f(K)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Uniform Continuity on Compact (9.25):} $E$ compact, $f:E\to\mathbb R^m$ continuous $\implies f$ uniformly continuous.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Dini's Theorem (9.40):} $K$ compact, $f_k:K\to\mathbb R$ ptwise monotone to continuous $f$ $\implies f_k\to f$ uniformly on $K$.

\section*{5. Differentiation in $\mathbb R^n$}
\textbf{Defs:} $f:V\to\mathbb R^m$, $V\subset\mathbb R^n$ open. $f$ diff at $a\in V$ $\iff$ $\exists$ linear $Df(a):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ s.t. $\lim_{h\to0}\frac{\|f(a+h)-f(a)-Df(a)h\|}{\|h\|}=0$. $Df(a)$ is the Jacobian. If $f=(f_1,\dots,f_m)$, then $Df=(J_{ij})$, $J_{ij}=\partial f_i/\partial x_j$.\\[-2pt]

Continuity $\not\Rightarrow$ Differentiability. $f$ diff at $a$ $\implies$ all partials exist and $f$ continuous.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Chain Rule (10.3):} $D(f\circ g)(a)=Df(g(a))Dg(a)$. Scalar: $\partial f/\partial x_i=\sum_j\frac{\partial f}{\partial u_j}\frac{\partial u_j}{\partial x_i}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Equality of Mixed Partials (10.6):} If $f_{xy}$ and $f_{yx}$ exist and are continuous at $(a,b)$, then $f_{xy}(a,b)=f_{yx}(a,b)$. If $f\in C^2$, then $f_{xy}=f_{yx}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Euler's Homogeneous Function Thm:} $f\in C^1$, homogeneous of degree $k$ ($f(tx)=t^kf(x)$) $\implies x\cdot\nabla f(x)=k f(x)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Mean Value Theorem:} $f:U\to\mathbb R$, $U$ open connected, $\|Df(x)\|\le M$ $\forall x\in U$ $\implies|f(x)-f(y)|\le M\|x-y\|$ $\forall x,y\in U$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Taylor's Theorem (10.14):} $f\in C^{k+1}$: $f(b)=f(a)+\sum_{j=1}^k\frac1{j!}(D^jf(a))(b-a)^j+\frac1{(k+1)!}(D^{k+1}f(c))(b-a)^{k+1}$ for some $c$ on $[a,b]$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Taylor 2nd Order, 2 vars:} $f(a+h,b+k)=f(a,b)+hf_x+kf_y+\frac12(h^2f_{xx}+2hkf_{xy}+k^2f_{yy})+o(h^2+k^2)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Inverse Function Theorem (11.6):} $f:V\to\mathbb R^n$, $C^1$, $V\subset\mathbb R^n$ open, $a\in V$, $Df(a)$ invertible $\implies\exists$ open $U\ni a$, $W\ni f(a)$: $f|_U$ is 1-1, $f(U)=W$, $f^{-1}\in C^1$ on $W$, and $Df^{-1}(f(x))=[Df(x)]^{-1}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Implicit Function Theorem (11.47):} $F=(F_1,\dots,F_n):V\to\mathbb R^n$, $V\subset\mathbb R^{n+p}$ open, $F\in C^1$. If $F(a,b)=0$, $a\in\mathbb R^n$, $b\in\mathbb R^p$, and $\det\frac{\partial(F_1,\dots,F_n)}{\partial(x_1,\dots,x_n)}(a,b)\neq0$, then $\exists$ open $W\subset\mathbb R^p$ containing $b$ and unique $C^1$ function $g:W\to\mathbb R^n$ with $g(b)=a$ and $F(g(t),t)=0$ $\forall t\in W$.

\section*{6. Integration in $\mathbb R^n$}
\textbf{Defs:} $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ bounded. Upper/lower Darboux sums: $U(P,f)=\sum M_i\Delta x_i$, $L(P,f)=\sum m_i\Delta x_i$. $f\in\mathcal R$ (Riemann integrable) $\iff\sup_P L(P,f)=\inf_P U(P,f)$. Equivalent: $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists P$ s.t. $U(P,f)-L(P,f)<\varepsilon$. $f$ continuous a.e. means discontinuities have measure zero.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Lebesgue's Theorem (9.49):} Bounded $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is Riemann integrable $\iff$ $f$ is continuous a.e.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Elementary Integrability:} Every monotone function on $[a,b]$ is Riemann integrable. Every step function is integrable. If $f\in\mathcal R$ and $g=f$ a.e., then $g\in\mathcal R$ and $\int g=\int f$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Integral Properties:} If $f,g\in\mathcal R[a,b]$, then $f+g$, $cf$, $|f|$, $\max(f,g)$, $\min(f,g)$, and $fg$ are all in $\mathcal R$. Also $|\int f|\le\int|f|$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{FTC:} $F\in C^1[a,b]$ and $F'=f$ a.e. with $f\in\mathcal R$ $\implies\int_a^b f=F(b)-F(a)$. Conversely, if $f\in\mathcal R[a,b]$ and $F(x)=\int_a^x f$, then $F$ is continuous and $F'(x)=f(x)$ a.e.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{MVT for Integrals:} $f\in\mathcal R[a,b]$, $m\le f\le M$ $\implies\exists c\in[a,b]$ with $\int_a^b f=(b-a)f(c)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Differentiating Under Integral (Thm 11.4):} $f(x,y)$ continuous on $[a,b]\times[c,d]\implies F(y)=\int_a^b f(x,y)dx$ continuous on $[c,d]$, and if $f_y$ exists and is continuous on $[a,b]\times[c,d]$, then $F'(y)=\int_a^b f_y(x,y)dx$.

\section*{7. Lebesgue Measure}
\textbf{Defs:} $E\subset\mathbb R$ has (outer) measure $m(E)=0$ if $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists$ countable cover $\{I_j\}$ by open intervals with $\sum|I_j|<\varepsilon$. A property holds \textbf{almost everywhere} (a.e.) if the set where it fails has measure zero. $f$ Lebesgue measurable: $\forall\alpha\in\mathbb R$, $\{f>\alpha\}$ is measurable. Lebesgue integral: $\int_E f=\sup\{\int_E\phi:0\le\phi\le f,\ \phi\text{ simple}\}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Null Sets (7.2):} Every countable set has measure zero. Finite/countable union of measure-zero sets has measure zero.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Monotone Convergence (MCT):} $f_k\ge0$ measurable, $f_k\uparrow f$ a.e. $\implies\int f_k\uparrow\int f$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Dominated Convergence (DCT):} $f_k\to f$ a.e., $|f_k|\le g$ with $g\in L^1\implies\int f_k\to\int f$. (Most commonly used.)\\![-2pt]

\textbf{Fatou's Lemma:} $f_k\ge0$ measurable $\implies\int\liminf f_k\le\liminf\int f_k$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Riemann $\iff$ Lebesgue + Measure Zero:} For bounded $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$: $f$ Riemann integrable $\iff$ $f$ is bounded a.e. In fact, bounded $f$ Riemann integrable $\iff$ $f$ is continuous a.e., and the two integrals agree.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{$L^p$ Spaces:} $\|f\|_p=(\int|f|^p)^{1/p}$, $1\le p<\infty$. H\"older: $\|fg\|_1\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q$, $\frac1p+\frac1q=1$. Minkowski: $\|f+g\|_p\le\|f\|_p+\|g\|_p$.

\section*{8. Key Formulas}
\textbf{Jacobian Matrix:} $Df(x)=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{\partial f_1}{\partial x_1}&\cdots&\frac{\partial f_1}{\partial x_n}\\\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\\frac{\partial f_m}{\partial x_1}&\cdots&\frac{\partial f_m}{\partial x_n}\end{pmatrix}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Gradient \& Hessian:} $\nabla f=(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1},\dots,\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_n})$. $H_f=D^2f=(\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j})$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Directional Derivative:} $D_u f(a)=\nabla f(a)\cdot u=\sum_i u_i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(a)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Laplacian:} $\Delta f=\nabla\cdot\nabla f=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i^2}$. $f$ harmonic: $\Delta f=0$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Polar Coordinates Jacobian:} $dx\,dy=r\,dr\,d\theta$. Spherical ($n=3$): $dx\,dy\,dz=\rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\phi\,d\theta$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Gamma Function:} $\Gamma(n+1)=n!$, $\Gamma(z+1)=z\Gamma(z)$, $\int_0^\infty t^{z-1}e^{-t}dt=\Gamma(z)$.

\section*{9. Convergence Tests Summary}
\textbf{Positive series} $\sum a_k$, $a_k\ge0$:
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|}
\hline
Test & Condition & Conclusion\\\hline
Comparison & $a_k\le b_k$ & $\sum b_k<\infty\implies\sum a_k<\infty$\\\hline
LCT & $L=\lim a_k/b_k$, $0<L<\infty$ & same conv as $\sum b_k$\\\hline
Integral & $f\ge0$ decr, $a_k=f(k)$ & $\int f<\infty\iff\sum a_k<\infty$\\\hline
Root & $r=\limsup a_k^{1/k}$ & $r<1\implies$conv; $r>1\implies$div\\\hline
Ratio & $r=\lim|a_{k+1}/a_k|$ & $r<1\implies$conv; $r>1\implies$div\\\hline
Raabe & $|a_{k+1}/a_k|\le1-p/k$ & $p>1\implies$abs conv\\\hline
\end{tabular}\\[4pt]
\textbf{Alternating series} $\sum(-1)^ka_k$, $a_k\downarrow0$: $|s-s_n|\le a_{n+1}$.\\[-2pt]
\textbf{Dirichlet's Test:} $\sum a_k$ partial sums bounded + $b_k\downarrow0$ $\implies\sum a_kb_k$ converges.\\[-2pt]
\textbf{Abel's Test:} $\sum a_k$ converges + $b_k$ monotone bounded $\implies\sum a_kb_k$ converges.

\section*{10. Quick Reference}
$\mathbb R^n$ Norms: $\|x\|_\infty=\max|x_i|$, $\|x\|_1=\sum|x_i|$, $\|x\|=\sqrt{\sum x_i^2}$.\\[-2pt]
$\|x\|_\infty\le\|x\|\le\sqrt n\|x\|_\infty$, $\|x\|\le\|x\|_1\le\sqrt n\|x\|$.\\[-2pt]
Conv in $\mathbb R^n$: $x_k^{(j)}\to a_j\ \forall j\iff x_k\to a$. Conv $\iff$ Cauchy. BW: bounded $\implies$ conv subseq.\\[-2pt]
Compactness: Compact $\iff$ closed + bounded. Compact $\implies$ uniformly continuous.\\[-2pt]
Continuous image of compact is compact (bounded, max/min exist).\\[-2pt]
Connectedness: $E\subset\mathbb R$ connected $\iff$ $E$ is an interval. Continuous image of connected set is connected.

\documentclass[8pt]{extarticle}
\usepackage[margin=0.15in, landscape, top=0.12in, bottom=0.12in, left=0.12in, right=0.12in]{geometry}
\usepackage{amsmath, amssymb, enumitem}
\usepackage{mathtools}
\usepackage{parskip}

\begin{document}
\setlength{\parskip}{-5pt}
\fontsize{6.5pt}{7.5pt}\selectfont
\addtolength{\baselineskip}{-1.5pt}
\setlength{\itemsep}{-5pt}
\setlength{\topsep}{-4pt}
\setlength{\partopsep}{0pt}
\setlength{\parsep}{-3pt}

\section*{1. Infinite Series of Real Numbers}
\textbf{Defs:} $s_n=\sum_{k=1}^n a_k$. $\sum a_k$ converges to $s$: $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists N:n\ge N\implies|s_n-s|<\varepsilon$. Diverges: $\{s_n\}$ has no limit. Abs conv: $\sum|a_k|<\infty$. Conditional: conv but not abs.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Divergence Test:} $a_k\not\to0\implies\sum a_k$ diverges.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Geometric:} $\sum_{k=0}^\infty x^k=\frac1{1-x}$ for $|x|<1$, diverges for $|x|\ge1$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Cauchy Criterion:} $\sum a_k$ conv $\iff\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists N:m\ge n\ge N\implies\sum_{k=n}^m a_k<\varepsilon$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Comparison:} $0\le a_k\le b_k$ for large $k$: $\sum b_k<\infty\implies\sum a_k<\infty$; $\sum a_k=\infty\implies\sum b_k=\infty$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{LCT:} $L=\lim a_k/b_k$, $b_k>0$. $0<L<\infty$: same conv. $L=0$+$\sum b_k<\infty\implies\sum a_k<\infty$. $L=\infty$+$\sum b_k=\infty\implies\sum a_k=\infty$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Integral Test:} $f\ge0$ decr on $[1,\infty)$. $\sum f(k)$ conv $\iff\int_1^\infty f<\infty$. $\sum1/k^p$ conv $\iff p>1$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Root Test:} $r=\limsup|a_k|^{1/k}$. $r<1\implies$abs conv; $r>1\implies$diverge.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Ratio Test:} $r=\lim|a_{k+1}/a_k|$. $r<1\implies$abs conv; $r>1\implies$diverge.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Abs Conv:} Abs conv $\implies$conv (converse false). $\sum(-1)^k/k$ cond converges.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Rearrangements:} If $\sum a_k$ abs conv, every rearrangement $\to$ same sum. Cond conv $\implies$ can rearrange to any $x\in\mathbb R\cup\{\pm\infty\}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Abel's Formula:} $A_{n,m}=\sum_{k=m}^n a_k$. $\sum_{k=m}^n a_kb_k=A_{n,m}b_n-\sum_{k=m}^{n-1}A_{k,m}(b_{k+1}-b_k)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Dirichlet's Test:} $\sum a_k$ partial sums bounded + $b_k\downarrow0$ $\implies\sum a_kb_k$ converges.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Alt Series Test:} $a_k\downarrow0\implies\sum(-1)^ka_k$ converges.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Alt Series Error:} $a_k\downarrow0$, $s=\sum(-1)^ka_k$, $|s-s_n|\le a_{n+1}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Integral Test Error:} $0\le\sum_{k=1}^n f(k)-\int_1^n f\le f(1)$. If $\sum f(k)$ conv: $0\le s-s_n+\int_n^\infty f\le f(n)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Logarithmic Test:} $p=\lim\frac{\log(1/|a_k|)}{\log k}$. $p>1\implies$abs conv; $p<1\implies$diverge.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Raabe's Test:} $|a_{k+1}/a_k|\le1-p/k+O(1/k)$ with $p>1\implies\sum a_k$ abs conv.

\section*{2. Infinite Series of Functions}
\textbf{Defs:} $f_n\to f$ ptwise: $\forall x\in E$, $\lim f_n(x)=f(x)$. Uniform: $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists N:n\ge N\implies|f_n(x)-f(x)|<\varepsilon\ \forall x\in E$ ($N$ depends only on $\varepsilon$, not $x$). Radius of conv $R$: series abs conv for $|x-x_0|<R$, diverges for $|x-x_0|>R$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Uniform $\Rightarrow$ Continuity:} $f_n\to f$ uniformly on $E$, each $f_n$ cont at $x_0\in E$ $\implies f$ cont at $x_0$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Uniform $\Rightarrow$ Integrability:} $f_n\to f$ uniformly on $[a,b]$, each integrable $\implies f$ integrable and $\int_a^b f_n\to\int_a^b f$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Uniform $\Rightarrow$ Differentiability:} $(a,b)$ bounded, $f_n$ diff on $(a,b)$, $f_n(x_0)$ converges for some $x_0$, $f_n'$ converges uniformly on $(a,b)\implies f_n\to f$ uniformly and $f'=\lim f_n'$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Uniform Cauchy Criterion:} $f_n$ conv uniformly on $E$ $\iff\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists N:n,m\ge N\implies|f_n(x)-f_m(x)|<\varepsilon\ \forall x\in E$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Weierstrass M-Test:} $|f_k(x)|\le M_k$ for $x\in E$, $\sum M_k<\infty\implies\sum f_k$ abs conv and uniformly on $E$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Term-by-Term Tests:} Uniform conv + each continuous $\implies\sum f_k$ continuous. On $[a,b]$, each integrable $\implies\int\sum f_k=\sum\int f_k$. Open interval, each diff, $\sum f_k$ conv at $x_0$, $\sum f_k'$ conv uniformly $\implies(\sum f_k)'=\sum f_k'$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Dirichlet's Test for Uniform Conv:} $|\sum_{k=1}^n f_k(x)|\le M$ for all $n,x\in E$ and $g_k\downarrow0$ uniformly $\implies\sum f_kg_k$ converges uniformly.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Power Series Radius:} $S(x)=\sum a_k(x-x_0)^k$, $R=1/\limsup|a_k|^{1/k}$. $S$ abs conv for $|x-x_0|<R$, uniformly on any $[a,b]\subset(x_0-R,x_0+R)$, diverges for $|x-x_0|>R$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{PS Diff \& Int:} On $(x_0-R,x_0+R)$, $S\in C^\infty$ and $S'(x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty k a_k(x-x_0)^{k-1}$, $\int S=\sum\frac{a_k}{k+1}(x-x_0)^{k+1}+C$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Abel's Theorem:} If $\sum a_k(x-x_0)^k$ converges on $[a,b]$, then it converges uniformly on $[a,b]$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Uniqueness:} If $f(x)=\sum a_k(x-x_0)^k$ on open interval $I$, then $a_k=f^{(k)}(x_0)/k!$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Binomial Series:} $|x|<1$, $(1+x)^\alpha=\sum_{k=0}^\infty\binom{\alpha}{k}x^k$, $\binom{\alpha}{k}=\frac{\alpha(\alpha-1)\cdots(\alpha-k+1)}{k!}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Key Series:} $e^x=\sum_{k=0}^\infty\frac{x^k}{k!}$, $\sin x=\sum_{k=0}^\infty\frac{(-1)^kx^{2k+1}}{(2k+1)!}$, $\cos x=\sum_{k=0}^\infty\frac{(-1)^kx^{2k}}{(2k)!}$, $\log(1+x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty\frac{(-1)^{k+1}x^k}{k}$, $|x|<1$.

\section*{3. Euclidean Spaces $\mathbb R^n$}

\textbf{Topological Definitions:}
\begin{itemize}[left=0pt, itemsep=0pt, topsep=0pt, parsep=0pt]
\item Open ball: $B_r(a)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x-a\|<r\}$. Closed ball: $\{\|x-a\|\le r\}$.
\item $V\subset\mathbb R^n$ is \textbf{open}: $\forall a\in V$, $\exists\varepsilon>0:B_\varepsilon(a)\subset V$.
\item $E$ is \textbf{closed}: $E^c$ is open.
\item \textbf{Relatively open in }$A$: $E\subset A$ is relatively open if $E=A\cap V$ for some open $V$.
\item \textbf{Relatively closed in }$A$: $E=A\cap F$ for some closed $F$.
\item \textbf{Compact}: every open cover has a finite subcover.
\item \textbf{Connected}: cannot be separated into two nonempty disjoint relatively-open sets.
\item \textbf{Interior} $E^\circ$: union of all open subsets of $E$ (largest open set $\subset E$).
\item \textbf{Closure} $\overline{E}$: intersection of all closed supersets of $E$ (smallest closed set $\supset E$).
\item \textbf{Boundary} $\partial E=\overline{E}\setminus E^\circ$.
\item \textbf{Limit point/accumulation point}: $x$ is limit point of $E$ if every $B_\varepsilon(x)$ contains $y\in E$ with $y\ne x$.
\item $E$ is \textbf{perfect}: $E$ is closed and every point of $E$ is a limit point of $E$.
\item \textbf{Dense}: $\overline{E}=\mathbb R^n$ (or $\overline{E}\cap U\neq\varnothing$ for every open $U$).
\item \textbf{Sequentially compact}: every sequence has a convergent subsequence.
\end{itemize}
\textbf{Cauchy-Schwarz:} $|x\cdot y|\le\|x\|\|y\|$, equality $\iff x,y$ parallel or one is zero.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Triangle Inequalities:} $\|x+y\|\le\|x\|+\|y\|$, $\|x-y\|\ge|\|x\|-\|y\||$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Norm Inequalities:} $\|x\|_\infty\le\|x\|\le\sqrt n\|x\|_\infty$, $\|x\|\le\|x\|_1\le\sqrt n\|x\|$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Heine-Borel:} $E\subset\mathbb R^n$ compact $\iff$ $E$ is closed and bounded.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Closed $\iff$ Sequential:} $E$ closed $\iff$ $x_k\in E$, $x_k\to x$ $\implies x\in E$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Limit Point Char:} $E$ closed $\iff$ $E$ contains all its limit points.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Open/Closed Properties:} Arbitrary unions of open are open; finite intersections of open are open. Arbitrary intersections of closed are closed; finite unions of closed are closed.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Connected $\iff$ Interval:} $E\subset\mathbb R$ connected $\iff$ $E$ is an interval. Rectangles in $\mathbb R^n$ are connected.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Linear Maps:} $T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ linear $\iff$ $T(x)=Bx$ for unique $m\times n$ matrix $B$. Operator norm: $\|T\|=\sup_{\|x\|=0}\frac{\|T(x)\|}{\|x\|}$, and $\|T(x)\|\le\|T\|\|x\|$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Cross Product:} $x,y\in\mathbb R^3$: $x\times y\perp x$ and $x\times y\perp y$. $\|x\times y\|=\|x\|\|y\|\sin\theta$. $x\times(y\times z)=(x\cdot z)y-(x\cdot y)z$.

\section*{4. Convergence in $\mathbb R^n$}
\textbf{Defs:} $x_k=(x_k^{(1)},\dots,x_k^{(n)})\to a=(a_1,\dots,a_n)\iff x_k^{(j)}\to a_j$ for each $j$. Bounded: $\exists M>0:\|x_k\|\le M\ \forall k$. Cauchy: $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists N:k,m\ge N\implies\|x_k-x_m\|<\varepsilon$.\\[-2pt]

$f(x)\to L$ as $x\to a$: $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists\delta>0:0<\|x-a\|<\delta\implies\|f(x)-L\|<\varepsilon$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Conv $\iff$ Componentwise:} $x_k^{(j)}\to a_j\ \forall j\iff x_k\to a$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Sequence Properties:} Uniqueness. Subseq $\to$ same limit. Conv $\implies$ bounded. Conv $\iff$ Cauchy.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Bolzano-Weierstrass:} Every bounded sequence in $\mathbb R^n$ has a convergent subsequence.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Limit Laws:} $\lim(f+g)=L+M$, $\lim(\alpha f)=\alpha L$, $\lim(f\cdot g)=L\cdot M$. Squeeze: $g\le h\le f$, $\lim f=\lim g=L\implies\lim h=L$. Composition: $\lim_{x\to a}g(x)=L$, $\lim_{y\to L}h(y)=M\implies\lim_{x\to a}h(g(x))=M$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Limit $\iff$ Sequential:} $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=L\iff f(x_k)\to L$ for every $x_k\to a$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Continuous $\iff$ Preimage of Open:} $f:E\to\mathbb R^m$ continuous $\iff$ $f^{-1}(V)$ relatively open in $E$ for every open $V\subset\mathbb R^m$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Compact $\Rightarrow$ Continuity:} $K$ compact, $f:K\to\mathbb R^m$ continuous on $K$ $\implies f(K)$ compact. Hence $f$ bounded and attains max/min (Extreme Value Thm).\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Continuity $\Rightarrow$ Connectedness:} $E$ connected, $f:E\to\mathbb R^m$ continuous $\implies f(E)$ is connected.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Continuous Inverse:} $K$ compact, $f:K\to\mathbb R^m$ is 1-1 and continuous $\implies f^{-1}$ continuous on $f(K)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Uniform Continuity on Compact:} $E$ compact, $f:E\to\mathbb R^m$ continuous $\implies f$ uniformly continuous.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Dini's Theorem:} $K$ compact, $f_k:K\to\mathbb R$ ptwise monotone to continuous $f$ $\implies f_k\to f$ uniformly on $K$.

\section*{5. Differentiation in $\mathbb R^n$}
\textbf{Defs:} $f:V\to\mathbb R^m$, $V\subset\mathbb R^n$ open. $f$ diff at $a\in V$ $\iff$ $\exists$ linear $Df(a):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ s.t. $\lim_{h\to0}\frac{\|f(a+h)-f(a)-Df(a)h\|}{\|h\|}=0$. $Df(a)$ is the Jacobian. If $f=(f_1,\dots,f_m)$, then $Df=(J_{ij})$, $J_{ij}=\partial f_i/\partial x_j$.\\[-2pt]

Continuity $\not\Rightarrow$ Differentiability. $f$ diff at $a$ $\implies$ all partials exist and $f$ continuous.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Chain Rule:} $D(f\circ g)(a)=Df(g(a))Dg(a)$. Scalar: $\partial f/\partial x_i=\sum_j\frac{\partial f}{\partial u_j}\frac{\partial u_j}{\partial x_i}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Equality of Mixed Partials:} If $f_{xy}$ and $f_{yx}$ exist and are continuous at $(a,b)$, then $f_{xy}(a,b)=f_{yx}(a,b)$. If $f\in C^2$, then $f_{xy}=f_{yx}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Euler's Homogeneous Function Thm:} $f\in C^1$, homogeneous of degree $k$ ($f(tx)=t^kf(x)$) $\implies x\cdot\nabla f(x)=k f(x)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Mean Value Theorem:} $f:U\to\mathbb R$, $U$ open connected, $\|Df(x)\|\le M$ $\forall x\in U$ $\implies|f(x)-f(y)|\le M\|x-y\|$ $\forall x,y\in U$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Taylor's Theorem:} $f\in C^{k+1}$: $f(b)=f(a)+\sum_{j=1}^k\frac1{j!}(D^jf(a))(b-a)^j+\frac1{(k+1)!}(D^{k+1}f(c))(b-a)^{k+1}$ for some $c$ on $[a,b]$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Taylor 2nd Order, 2 vars:} $f(a+h,b+k)=f(a,b)+hf_x+kf_y+\frac12(h^2f_{xx}+2hkf_{xy}+k^2f_{yy})+o(h^2+k^2)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Inverse Function Theorem:} $f:V\to\mathbb R^n$, $C^1$, $V\subset\mathbb R^n$ open, $a\in V$, $Df(a)$ invertible $\implies\exists$ open $U\ni a$, $W\ni f(a)$: $f|_U$ is 1-1, $f(U)=W$, $f^{-1}\in C^1$ on $W$, and $Df^{-1}(f(x))=[Df(x)]^{-1}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Implicit Function Theorem:} $F=(F_1,\dots,F_n):V\to\mathbb R^n$, $V\subset\mathbb R^{n+p}$ open, $F\in C^1$. If $F(a,b)=0$, $a\in\mathbb R^n$, $b\in\mathbb R^p$, and $\det\frac{\partial(F_1,\dots,F_n)}{\partial(x_1,\dots,x_n)}(a,b)\neq0$, then $\exists$ open $W\subset\mathbb R^p$ containing $b$ and unique $C^1$ function $g:W\to\mathbb R^n$ with $g(b)=a$ and $F(g(t),t)=0$ $\forall t\in W$.

\section*{6. Integration in $\mathbb R^n$}
\textbf{Defs:} $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ bounded. Upper/lower Darboux sums: $U(P,f)=\sum M_i\Delta x_i$, $L(P,f)=\sum m_i\Delta x_i$. $f\in\mathcal R$ (Riemann integrable) $\iff\sup_P L(P,f)=\inf_P U(P,f)$. Equivalent: $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists P$ s.t. $U(P,f)-L(P,f)<\varepsilon$. $f$ continuous a.e. means discontinuities have measure zero.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Lebesgue's Theorem:} Bounded $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is Riemann integrable $\iff$ $f$ is continuous a.e.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Elementary Integrability:} Every monotone function on $[a,b]$ is Riemann integrable. Every step function is integrable. If $f\in\mathcal R$ and $g=f$ a.e., then $g\in\mathcal R$ and $\int g=\int f$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Integral Properties:} If $f,g\in\mathcal R[a,b]$, then $f+g$, $cf$, $|f|$, $\max(f,g)$, $\min(f,g)$, and $fg$ are all in $\mathcal R$. Also $|\int f|\le\int|f|$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{FTC:} $F\in C^1[a,b]$ and $F'=f$ a.e. with $f\in\mathcal R$ $\implies\int_a^b f=F(b)-F(a)$. Conversely, if $f\in\mathcal R[a,b]$ and $F(x)=\int_a^x f$, then $F$ is continuous and $F'(x)=f(x)$ a.e.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{MVT for Integrals:} $f\in\mathcal R[a,b]$, $m\le f\le M$ $\implies\exists c\in[a,b]$ with $\int_a^b f=(b-a)f(c)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Differentiating Under Integral:} $f(x,y)$ continuous on $[a,b]\times[c,d]\implies F(y)=\int_a^b f(x,y)dx$ continuous on $[c,d]$, and if $f_y$ exists and is continuous on $[a,b]\times[c,d]$, then $F'(y)=\int_a^b f_y(x,y)dx$.

\section*{7. Lebesgue Measure}
\textbf{Defs:} $E\subset\mathbb R$ has (outer) measure $m(E)=0$ if $\forall\varepsilon>0$, $\exists$ countable cover $\{I_j\}$ by open intervals with $\sum|I_j|<\varepsilon$. A property holds \textbf{almost everywhere} (a.e.) if the set where it fails has measure zero. $f$ Lebesgue measurable: $\forall\alpha\in\mathbb R$, $\{f>\alpha\}$ is measurable. Lebesgue integral: $\int_E f=\sup\{\int_E\phi:0\le\phi\le f,\ \phi\text{ simple}\}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Null Sets:} Every countable set has measure zero. Finite/countable union of measure-zero sets has measure zero.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Monotone Convergence (MCT):} $f_k\ge0$ measurable, $f_k\uparrow f$ a.e. $\implies\int f_k\uparrow\int f$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Dominated Convergence (DCT):} $f_k\to f$ a.e., $|f_k|\le g$ with $g\in L^1\implies\int f_k\to\int f$. (Most commonly used.)\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Fatou's Lemma:} $f_k\ge0$ measurable $\implies\int\liminf f_k\le\liminf\int f_k$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Riemann $\iff$ Lebesgue + Measure Zero:} For bounded $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$: $f$ Riemann integrable $\iff$ $f$ is bounded a.e. In fact, bounded $f$ Riemann integrable $\iff$ $f$ is continuous a.e., and the two integrals agree.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{$L^p$ Spaces:} $\|f\|_p=(\int|f|^p)^{1/p}$, $1\le p<\infty$. H\"older: $\|fg\|_1\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q$, $\frac1p+\frac1q=1$. Minkowski: $\|f+g\|_p\le\|f\|_p+\|g\|_p$.

\section*{8. Formulas}
\textbf{Jacobian Matrix:} $Df(x)=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{\partial f_1}{\partial x_1}&\cdots&\frac{\partial f_1}{\partial x_n}\\\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\\frac{\partial f_m}{\partial x_1}&\cdots&\frac{\partial f_m}{\partial x_n}\end{pmatrix}$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Gradient \& Hessian:} $\nabla f=(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1},\dots,\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_n})$. $H_f=D^2f=(\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j})$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Directional Derivative:} $D_u f(a)=\nabla f(a)\cdot u=\sum_i u_i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(a)$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Laplacian:} $\Delta f=\nabla\cdot\nabla f=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i^2}$. $f$ harmonic: $\Delta f=0$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Polar Coordinates Jacobian:} $dx\,dy=r\,dr\,d\theta$. Spherical ($n=3$): $dx\,dy\,dz=\rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\phi\,d\theta$.\\[-2pt]

\textbf{Gamma Function:} $\Gamma(n+1)=n!$, $\Gamma(z+1)=z\Gamma(z)$, $\int_0^\infty t^{z-1}e^{-t}dt=\Gamma(z)$.

\section*{9. Convergence Tests}
\textbf{Positive series} $\sum a_k$, $a_k\ge0$:
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|}
\hline
Test & Condition & Conclusion\\\hline
Comparison & $a_k\le b_k$ & $\sum b_k<\infty\implies\sum a_k<\infty$\\\hline
LCT & $L=\lim a_k/b_k$, $0<L<\infty$ & same conv as $\sum b_k$\\\hline
Integral & $f\ge0$ decr, $a_k=f(k)$ & $\int f<\infty\iff\sum a_k<\infty$\\\hline
Root & $r=\limsup a_k^{1/k}$ & $r<1\implies$conv; $r>1\implies$div\\\hline
Ratio & $r=\lim|a_{k+1}/a_k|$ & $r<1\implies$conv; $r>1\implies$div\\\hline
Raabe & $|a_{k+1}/a_k|\le1-p/k$ & $p>1\implies$abs conv\\\hline
\end{tabular}\\[4pt]
\textbf{Alternating series} $\sum(-1)^ka_k$, $a_k\downarrow0$: $|s-s_n|\le a_{n+1}$.\\[-2pt]
\textbf{Dirichlet's Test:} $\sum a_k$ partial sums bounded + $b_k\downarrow0$ $\implies\sum a_kb_k$ converges.\\[-2pt]
\textbf{Abel's Test:} $\sum a_k$ converges + $b_k$ monotone bounded $\implies\sum a_kb_k$ converges.

\section*{10. Quick Reference}
$\mathbb R^n$ Norms: $\|x\|_\infty=\max|x_i|$, $\|x\|_1=\sum|x_i|$, $\|x\|=\sqrt{\sum x_i^2}$.\\[-2pt]
$\|x\|_\infty\le\|x\|\le\sqrt n\|x\|_\infty$, $\|x\|\le\|x\|_1\le\sqrt n\|x\|$.\\[-2pt]
Conv in $\mathbb R^n$: $x_k^{(j)}\to a_j\ \forall j\iff x_k\to a$. Conv $\iff$ Cauchy. BW: bounded $\implies$ conv subseq.\\[-2pt]
Compactness: Compact $\iff$ closed + bounded. Compact $\implies$ uniformly continuous.\\[-2pt]
Continuous image of compact is compact (bounded, max/min exist).\\[-2pt]
Connectedness: $E\subset\mathbb R$ connected $\iff$ $E$ is an interval. Continuous image of connected set is connected.

\end{document}
